title: Marguerite and the Orchard
premise: Marine biologist Ines Galloway has spent eleven years in the fading seaside town of Orchard's End, cataloguing sea turtles and keeping every relationship at arm's length—especially with Marguerite Voss, the orchard keeper who has loved them quietly for a decade. When a storm unearths a letter Ines wrote and never sent, postmarked eleven years ago, confessing everything they felt before fleeing town, Marguerite finally learns the truth: Ines left not from indifference but from terror of being known. As Ines accepts a research post abroad that departs on the last train of the season, they must choose between the safe invisibility they've perfected and staying in a life where someone truly sees them. The novel ends with Ines missing the train deliberately, standing in the orchard at dawn, choosing belonging over survival.
about_author: Mirabel Halloran is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where everyone knows everyone's business except their own. She lives within earshot of a lighthouse and believes every heart is trainable, given enough seasons.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Establishes Ines's meticulous, contained life at the marine station: nesting surveys, routines, and careful distance from townsfolk. Marguerite delivers apples to the station, and their easy warmth unsettles Ines more than any storm. Emotional beat: comfort that is also captivity—we see how invisibility protects and starves Ines at once.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keeper
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We learn Marguerite has tended both her family orchard and her decade-long hope, reading Ines's silences as answers. A town festival forces them together; Marguerite almost speaks, then doesn't. Emotional beat: loyalty to patience curdling into self-deception—the cost of waiting without asking.

chapters.title: What the Storm Dug Up
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A nor'easter erodes the dunes behind the old Galloway cottage, and Ines finds a weatherproofed tin containing an unsent letter written eleven years ago, addressed to Marguerite. The confession inside stops Ines cold. Emotional beat: dread and vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried, survival strategies exposed as cowardice.

chapters.title: Eleven Years, Postmarked
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Ines, unable to destroy or deliver the letter, leaves it half-hidden in the orchard's packing shed; Marguerite finds it while storing crates. Reading it alone among bare trees, she learns Ines once loved her and fled. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together—truth arriving years too late, loyalty suddenly a question.

chapters.title: The Cold Shoulder of Autumn
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marguerite goes quiet, returning Ines's distance with interest; Ines, offered a prestigious research post in Lisbon departing on the season's last train, begins packing as escape disguised as ambition. Each misreads the other's silence. Emotional beat: rising tension through avoidance—two people loyal to their wounds instead of each other.

chapters.title: Turtle Season Ends
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The final nest hatches; watching hatchlings race the gulls toward water, Ines confronts what survival instinct costs. A near-drowning rescue during a survey forces Ines into Marguerite's arms, literally, breaking the standoff. Emotional beat: the body's honesty overriding trained containment—fear of loss outgrowing fear of being seen.

chapters.title: Confrontation Among the Bare Trees
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite demands why Ines let her wait eleven years on a letter never sent. Ines defends invisibility as the only way to survive leaving home the first time; Marguerite names it cruelty dressed as kindness. Emotional beat: climax of the loyalty-vs-truth theme—love declared as accusation, neither willing to yield first.

chapters.title: The Last Train of the Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Departure day. Ines boards with packed bags and a rehearsed future, but the unsent letter—now annotated in Marguerite's hand, answering every line across eleven years—sits in their coat pocket. At the platform, the whistle blows. Emotional beat: peak crisis—the train as all of Ines's old exits arriving at once.

chapters.title: Staying After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Ines steps off as the doors close, walks the dark road to the orchard, and reads Marguerite's annotations aloud under the oldest tree: her answers, her anger, her unforgiven but persistent love. They fight, weep, and finally tell the truth face to face. Emotional beat: catharsis—belonging chosen consciously, not defaulted into.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue in early spring. Ines declines Lisbon by letter and takes a post at the regional station instead; together they graft new stock onto the orchard's oldest trees. The unsent letter is buried beneath a sapling, finally allowed to rest. Emotional beat: resolution—the price of survival paid back in full, and belonging planted where the truth was dug up.
